neighbours.label: A hanging or flowing garment and its lower edge: hem, hemline, skirt, dress, gown, robes (not collars, cuffs or jackets, and not 'hem' as hesitation)
fire: Mud had splashed the hem of her skirt during the walk.
The bride's gown trailed a metre behind her along the aisle.
He let down the hem so the trousers would reach his shoes.
The monks wore coarse brown robes tied with a rope.
Her pleated skirt swung as she climbed the steps.
A simple linen dress hung on the back of the door.
The tailor pinned the hemline just below the knee.
Silk evening dresses in every colour filled the costume department.
quiet: Mud had splashed the sleeve of her jacket during the walk.
The bride's veil lifted a little in the breeze along the aisle.
He tightened the belt so the trousers would stay up.
The monks wore sandals and carried wooden bowls.
Her wool scarf fluttered as she climbed the steps.
A simple straw hat hung on the back of the door.
The tailor pinned the collar just below the chin.
Leather boots in every size filled the costume department.
